ai.description: The Garden Flying Snake reaches 1.2 meters. It features a black-reticulated green body with vibrant red or orange vertebral spots and a yellow belly. It glides by flattening its ribs into a concave shape.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chrysopelea paradisi* is best distinguished by the vibrant red or orange vertebral spots along its back, which are absent in other *Chrysopelea* species found in India.
ai.habitat: The paradise flying snake inhabits tropical rainforests and moist deciduous forests, typically residing in the canopy at low to moderate elevations across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The paradise tree snake glides between trees by flattening its body into a concave shape, allowing it to perform controlled aerial maneuvers to escape predators or hunt.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chrysopelea paradisi* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–11 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (roughly March to August).
ai.distributionRemarks: The paradise tree snake occurs across the Western Ghats and Northeast India, typically inhabiting lowland forests and plantations up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
